page.overview:
What is Aiel Waste?

The Aiel Waste is a desert region named for the Aiel people who live there. The Aiel themselves refer to it as the Three-fold Land.

The Waste is bordered to the west by the Spine of the World, beyond which lie the Westlands; to the east by the Cliffs of Dawn and Great Rift, beyond which lies Shara; to the south by the Termool, beyond which lies the Drowned Lands and the Sea of Storms; and to the north by the Mountains of Dhoom, beyond which lies the Great Blight. Save for the uninhabited Termool, it is entirely landlocked.

Nothing is known about the Waste before the Breaking of the World, though it was likely very different. The geography surrounding the Waste appears to have been affected by major and unnatural geological events resulting in features such as the Great Rift and Cliffs of Dawn. While leaving the Waste, Rand saw a city with what appears to be docks hanging from the mountainside. These events doubtless contributed to the extreme dryness of the region. See climate.

The Aiel call the Waste the "Three-fold Land," referring to the three purposes of the Waste in Aiel culture: an anvil or "shaping stone" to make them, a testing ground to prove their worth, and a punishment for their sin. Aiel prophecy stated that the Aiel would leave the Waste once the Stone of Tear falls. Few Aiel had crossed the Spine of the World since they entered the Waste, until the Aiel War.. But this is clearly false. Aiel crossed to gift Avendoraldera roughly 500 years before the Aiel War. And for what it's worth, Stedding Tsofu seemed accustomed to Aiel visitors when Rand's party visited.}}
